institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A combination of personal development, excellent academic opportunities and exploring a new language.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good academic opportunities, beautiful nature and not very far from home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. We got a lot of emails all the time with necessary information. You had to keep track of it all, but it really helped. You could always just write an email to the university if you were in any doubt.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance in form of an intro week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I really recommend using
hybel.no
!!
You have to write to a lot of people, but I ended up in a really nice place.
Nordic students don't get offered to live in student accommodation, so we have to find something on our own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived close to campus, so I'm probably not the right to say.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't any available since we're from the Nordic countries, but it was manageable to find your own. The private housings usually like to have Danish people since we understand each other without them having to speak English in their own home.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up for courses on Studentweb. You can sign up for as many as you want until 15th of September (in my case). If you aren't sure about your courses, it is better to have too many at this point. Afterwards, you can deregister from the courses you aren't going to take. I found it very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always text both the course coordinator and the exchange office at NTNU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt about 2 courses, register to both. You can always deregister, but you cannot register to a new one after the deadline.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses had very varying difficulty. I mostly liked the subjects, but I haven't been very lucky with the lecturers.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
BA course: Much details compared to it being a BA-course. But we could bring notes to the exam, so it was alright.
MA courses: One had appropriate level for it being a MA-course, and the other was easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very much the same. Lectures, group work, presentations...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Neuroscience.
Immunology.
Pharmaceutical Innovation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would actually recommend all of them. Although, there are some things to think about before choosing them.

Neuroscience: A very good and thorough BA-course. Has a lot of details and is really not just an introductory course. Also, the lecturers were online - you never met the other people in the course. This might have changed, but for me, it was online. It was nice because then you could go on trips and then rewatch the lectures afterwards, but also sad because you didn't get to meet other people.

Immunology: A MA-course. Very difficult with lots of details, but I actually learned a lot. Definitely a good course if you're interested in immunology.

Pharmaceutical Innovation: A course describing the process from finding a drug to getting it approved to the market (going through preclinical tests and clinical trials). Mostly, it was very nice and very cool to get to know the process. Sometimes it was a bit challenging, because it's a MA-course on the pharmacy master, so they know a lot more about pharmaceuticals than us. But very nice with the overview.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying warmer clothes.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is very expensive even though the Norwegian crown is low right now. Just be prepared.

Clothes are less expensive, due to the Norwegian crown.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Trondheim is a very student-friendly city!!! It has gyms on the campus that you can buy a membership in very cheap when you are a student. You can also be a part of NTNUI where you can participate in sports also very cheap!! There is Studentersamfundet which is a collection of all student bars/cafés in Copenhagen, just in one. This is a nice place to be. You can volunteer in a lot of places as well. ESN Trondheim is also very nice to participate in. They plan a lot of events and trips (to e.g. Lofoten) that you can join very cheap. Here, you get to know a lot of other exchange students!! Trondheim is just amazing for students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Athletic: For sure Sit-training and NTNUI.
Social activities: ESN Trondheim plans a lot all the time!!
There are just a look of associations that you can join; I don't know all of them. But they'll tell you more about it in the introduction week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
NTNUI classes: You get to be active and meet other students. Both Norwegian students and exchange students. Very cheap.
NTNUI Koiene: They have cabins close to Trondheim that you can rent for 30 DKK. They usually are located in very nice surroundings. They have no electricity nor water, so be prepared for that. 
ESN Trondheim: They plan all your trips, so you don't have to yourself. You meet so many nice people!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Bymarka. Take the ferry to Fosen. Try one of the NTNUI cabins. Go to Gløshaugen and watch over the city. Just walk around in the city, experience the atmosphere.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Norwegians are a lot like us.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with them! They are much easier to talk with if they are forced to talk to you haha.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The student environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open!
Participate in as many social activities as you can!
Speak with some Norwegian people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very dark in the winter. Bring D-vitamin :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Definitely all the trips and experiences I've had with people from all over the world.
And getting to know my Norwegian roommates. It has been amazing!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
